Subject: Serving modes checklist & pricing asks

Hi Emma / Liam —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good session and great context on your MVP goals. Quick recap and a short checklist so we can send a clean comparison (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem) and a simple cost model for each path. Please confirm the three shaded items below so we can finalize numbers:

Workload summary (as I heard it):
- Expected steady-state: ~8 QPS (production baseline)
- Peak bursts: up to ~50 QPS for short windows (10–15% of traffic)
- Latency target: 95th < 200 ms for interactive flows
- Data residency: US-only for now; SOC 2 and basic IP restrictions required

Please confirm / correct:
1) Average tokens per request we should model (input + output) — I used 300 as a placeholder.
2) Typical monthly active users (or monthly requests) if you have a ballpark.
3) Any hard constraint that forces Private VPC/on-prem (legal/regulatory) vs 'preference' for VPC.

What we'll produce next (deliverables):
- Short pricing matrix (per-token Hosted estimate, equivalent per-token economics on Reserved Dedicated, Private VPC cost components).
- 12-month commit breakeven math for a couple of commit sizes.
- Draft SOW and a sample config for a pilot (we'll attach a SOW draft and pricing spreadsheet).

Attachments: pricing-model.xlsx (draft) — I'll send the filled numbers once you confirm the three items above.

Next steps: if the checklist looks right, can we schedule a 30-min follow-up Wed or Thu next week to walk the numbers? I proposed Wed 10/14 at 10:00 AM PT — works for you?

Thanks — talk soon.

Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Evelyn — good recap. Quick answers below and I've attached our short MVP requirements doc (Quantenix-MVP-requirements.pdf) for context.

Answers:
- Average tokens per request: 275 (we expect prompts ~100 tokens, model outputs ~175 tokens).
- Monthly requests: rough target 1.5M requests / month for the MVP (ramping to 4–5M over 6–9 months).
- Bursts: Peaks are usually marketing-driven (campaigns), expect short spikes up to ~50 QPS, rarely sustained more than an hour.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; data must remain in the US. We prefer a VPC/private deployment long-term because of the data policy, but we can pilot on Hosted if the migration path is clean.

Two asks for your pricing matrix:
1) Show per-token comparison (hosted) vs reserved capacity (monthly commit) — include break-even point.
2) Show the one-time and recurring costs for Private VPC (setup, infra, ongoing support).

Wed 10/14 10:00 AM PT works for me. Looking forward to the matrix — that will help our procurement.

—Emma

Subject: Re: Serving modes checklist & pricing asks — cost sketch + options

Emma — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the requirements doc. I filled the pricing-model.xlsx with two scenarios and a sample 12-month commit projection; summary below so you have a high-level view before the call on Wed.

Assumptions used (from your note):
- Avg tokens/request: 275
- Target month 0: 1.5M requests (~412.5M tokens/month)
- Steady-state QPS: ~8, peak ~50 (bursts ~10–15% of time)

High-level cost sketches (ballpark, USD):
1) Hosted API (no commit) — simplest to run a PoC
   - Per-token pricing (example): $0.000015 per token generated (bundled input + output adjustment in sheet)
   - Estimated cost for MVP month: ~ $6,200 (this covers average traffic; spikes increase cost linearly)
   - Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra setup; Cons: higher unit cost at scale, limited network isolation compared to VPC

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — best when sustained throughput
   - Example commit tiers in sheet: small commit ($20k/mo), medium ($45k/mo), large ($80k/mo)
   - At the medium tier ($45k/mo) your effective per-token cost drops ~3–4x vs Hosted when utilization is steady.
   - Break-even: with your projected token volumes, a medium commit breaks even vs Hosted between months 4–7 depending on ramp. Exact math in pricing-model.xlsx
   - Pros: predictable cost, lower per-token; Cons: upfront commit, capacity planning needed for burst headroom (we provide burst pool options)

3) Private VPC / on-prem — for regulatory requirements
   - One-time setup & integration: estimate ~$14k–$20k (networking, KMS, onboarding)
   - Monthly infra + support: estimate ~$30k–$40k/mo (depends on instance type and redundancy)
   - This option has the highest initial op overhead but gives full network control and data locality.

Suggested paths (pick one):
A) PoC on Hosted for 1–3 months to validate prompts and traffic, then switch to a medium Dedicated commit for production (we do stateful cache migration and pin model versions to reduce regression risk).
B) Start pilot on medium Dedicated commit (6-month minimum) if procurement needs predictable monthly spend from day 1.
C) If legal requires VPC, plan a Private VPC kickoff in parallel and use Hosted for short pilot while the VPC setup finishes.

Next steps I've attached: pricing-model.xlsx (filled with the numbers above) and a SOW template (SOW-draft.docx) — both in the drive link and attached to this thread. For the call on Wed 10/14 10:00 AM PT I will bring: an AE, a solutions engineer (Karthik), and a draft canary config for Dedicated that covers burst handling.

Please confirm which path you prefer and whether you want us to prep a 6-month vs 12-month commit comparison in the sheet.

Thanks — talk soon.
